headline: Highest risk is compliance/data leakage from Rasa handling text/voice over allowlisted egress; Marker is local-only and cannot directly inject or conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, so it cannot directly feed instructions into Rasa except through manual copy/paste or external bridging. Rasa does expose chat channels, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or automatic ingestion path, so the pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Marker output into a Rasa channel or prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw Marker output into Rasa without sanitizing.
Add a provenance tag to any transferred text.
Use a fixed template for handoff messages.
requires-engineering: add an isolation layer or broker with content filtering.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker is local-only with no network egress, while Rasa handles text and voice and can send data through allowlisted external channels. If both touch the same documents or transcripts, Rasa can leak content beyond the local environment even though Marker itself does not exfiltrate. The pairwise risk is therefore real but not default-critical.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are copied into Rasa conversations or training data, those contents can traverse Rasa channels.
IF Rasa is connected to any listed API channel, text or voice content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive text into Rasa channels.
Restrict Rasa to non-sensitive test data.
Review allowlisted integrations before enabling them.
Separate datasets used by Marker and Rasa.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound Rasa integrations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot contend with Rasa over shared mutable resources. Rasa also does not advertise filesystem write or git mutation here, only allowlisted network egress and multiple-instance limits. With no overlapping write surface, conflict is unlikely.
conditions: IF Rasa is wrapped with an external filesystem-writing tool, write conflict risk increases.
IF a shared mutable workspace is introduced, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid shared git repositories for handoffs.
Run each agent in its own directory.
Disable external write tools around Rasa.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text by Rasa if handed off directly. Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on conversational inputs, so unverified Marker output could cascade into incorrect replies or actions. The interaction is inferred, but the default handoff path is plausible.
conditions: IF Marker output is used as Rasa training or response content without review, errors can propagate.
IF Rasa is configured to answer customers from upstream summaries, it may repeat mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require source citations in Marker output.
Use confidence thresholds before Rasa consumes text.
Limit Rasa to draft-only mode for transferred content.
requires-engineering: add verification logic before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Marker is open-source document processing with no stated residency controls, while Rasa handles text and voice and can route data through external messaging APIs. If regulated content such as customer transcripts or documents flows from Marker into Rasa channels, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a violation, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer text or voice data is routed through Rasa integrations, compliance obligations apply.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments, mismatch risk materializes.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Block regulated data from external channels.
Document retention settings for each integration.
Verify residency for each connected API.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
